openQuestions.q: Does CHK-003's hard-blocking DONE gate for dev_memory_finish_decision conflict with the pre-existing playbook-runtime-memory-consumption-execution-plan.md M8 design, which specifies the same capture-or-noop decision as an ADVISORY reminder, and with that plan's Non-Goal 'Do not make every advisory reminder a hard blocker'? B-a7c5's decision.json explicitly overrides the dev-memory entry's own generic gateEvidence:false/authority:non_authoritative framing, but does not cite or reconcile with this specific pre-existing M8 milestone text or its Non-Goals/Acceptance-Table rows.
openQuestions.evidence: M8 tests: 'missing decision is visible in runbook/advisory output; no-op decision is accepted with reason'. Non-Goals: 'Do not make every advisory reminder a hard blocker.' Acceptance table: 'No evidence confusion | All packs remain gateEvidence:false and authority:non_authoritative.' B-a7c5 decision.json: 'This is a deliberate, explicit override of the artifact's own self-declared authority: non_authoritative / gateEvidence: false fields ... record this override explicitly in code comments so it isn't mistaken for a bug later.'
openQuestions.resolution: Deliberate, recorded escalation, not an accidental conflict. playbook-runtime-memory-consumption-execution-plan.md M8 shipped the dev_memory_finish_decision MECHANISM (command + record shape) as advisory-only, but never wired any CONSUMER to treat its absence as blocking -- that gap is exactly what this story closes. The escalation is scoped narrowly (this ONE command's presence, for THIS ONE consumer, the DONE gate) and stays inside Non-Goal #4's actual boundary ('do not let dev-memory or playbooks satisfy... DONE... evidence gates') because the gate requires a RECORD OF REFLECTION having happened, not that any LESSON's content be treated as proof of correctness -- structurally identical to summary_set, an existing required attestation that is not itself code-correctness evidence. plan.md's Reconciliation section documents this in full, and the spec doc itself will be updated (CHK-003 sub-task 6) to describe the delivered, escalated behavior rather than leaving the original advisory-only M8 text as a misleading stale description.

openQuestions.q: Does playbook-runtime-memory-consumption-execution-plan.md section 4.3's requirement that 'registered blocking consumers must expose an operator-visible bypass or downgrade path with a reason' apply to CHK-001's new DEV-entry blocking gate (dev-memory-preflight-ack)? If it applies, CHK-001 as scoped has no defer/skip-with-reason path analogous to CHK-003's defer-with-reason -- an operator whose preflight-pack build itself genuinely fails has no documented way to proceed past the gate. If section 4.3 is scoped only to the Active Playbook Runtime specifically (not artifact-existence gates like CHK-001), no action is needed.
openQuestions.evidence: 'registered blocking consumers must expose an operator-visible bypass or downgrade path with a reason; unregistered playbooks, candidate playbooks, and caller-provided policy fields cannot create blocking behavior.'
